delivered.migration: Additive migration 0028 persists per-video runtime stage state, independent lane state, append-only accepted units, append-only runtime events, and a superseded-contract registry with a write fence over generation_sessions, session_gpu_bindings, session_gpu_revalidations, global_queue_entries, compute_run_plans, pod_lifecycle_attempts, pod_dispatch_authorizations, and durable_generation_outputs.
delivered.admission_gate: A runtime row can only leave QUEUED when its generation request carries a durable admission, so CPU preparation, lane dispatch, and render are database-fenced behind fair admission rather than application convention.
delivered.lane_dispatch_gate: A lane may bind an attempt only when its own durable items manifest exists, exactly one predispatch authority row exists for that attempt, the attempt belongs to the same tenant lane and revision, and the attempt covers exactly the unaccepted planned units.
delivered.accepted_unit_resume: Accepted units are append-only facts of the video and lane, joined to live tenant artifact commit receipts inside the attempt output prefix, so a bounded retry generates only the remaining units and can never discard accepted output.
delivered.asset_barrier: Render cannot begin until every lane state is SUCCEEDED, and a complete video requires a durable render manifest plus final output hash.
delivered.truthful_states: The runtime exposes QUEUED, PREPARING, WAITING_FOR_WORKER, INITIALIZING, GENERATING_IMAGES, GENERATING_AVATAR, RENDERING, COMPLETE, FAILED, and CANCELED as durable observations, each carrying providerCallsAuthorized=false and authorizedSpendUsd=0. No state is synthesized ahead of a durable fact.
delivered.application_composition: apps/web/src/server/runtime/node-video-runtime.ts composes the migrated PGlite control plane, FairAdmissionRepository, VideoRuntimeService, ServerlessDispatchService, the fake per-lane Serverless v3 transports, the existing provider-free transcript/scheduler/prompt foundations, and tenant-private artifact commit receipts into one end-to-end provider-free video lifecycle.
delivered.runtime_firewall: scripts/verify-v2-05-runtime-firewall.mjs (wired into pnpm ci:static) proves the active runtime graph names no superseded table, GPU pair, Pod lifecycle control, queue purge, /workspace model mount, or compatibility escape hatch; that object keys derive only from trusted tenant lineage; that migration 0028 fences every registered superseded contract; and that no production source outside the explicit compatibility allowlist writes a superseded table.
delivered.application_surface: Generating a video registers its durable runtime; the private fair-queue view reports each owned video's factual stage and lane facts from the control plane instead of the superseded global-session projection; two owned-video routes advance and cancel exactly one video; and the approved queue design is unchanged apart from the stage sub-label now reading the runtime vocabulary. No compute control was introduced.
delivered.superseded_route_gate: Every superseded global-session surface (view, cancel, advance, project orchestration, download, and the v1 queue mutations) now requires explicit fixture control, so no ordinary production route, flag, or UI action reaches one. The firewall asserts the gate on each route.

not_delivered_by_design: The superseded global-session compatibility executor still exists in the application build output. It is fenced at the database boundary, excluded from the V2-05 active runtime graph, and every one of its HTTP surfaces now requires explicit fixture control, but the code itself is retained because it still carries the only proven final-MP4 render, playback, and download evidence. Removing it belongs with the checkpoint that reproduces that evidence on the V2-05 runtime.

The superseded shared-app view still declares GPU offer inventory, locked-pair, and orchestration fields. They are unreachable from ordinary production paths and no screen reads them, but the schema and type deletion waits for the executor removal above.

The V2-05 runtime completes a video against a durable render manifest and final output hash; it does not yet produce the reviewable MP4 artifact and download route that the compatibility executor still provides.
Hosted R2, non-superuser Neon row level security, published worker images or endpoints, live Serverless delivery, lane timing, billing, and physical worker drain remain later checkpoints.
